headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: caveman’s MCP/file workflows can ingest ai-engineering-hub content, while both profiles lack isolation details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman explicitly uses MCP and file-based inputs, so if ai-engineering-hub content is copied into those channels it could be treated as instructions. ai-engineering-hub is docs-only and runnable:false, so the interaction is inferred rather than observed; uncertainty pushes this above low. Both profiles show no provenance controls.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is placed into caveman's CLAUDE.md, docs/, or another MCP-visible file
IF caveman parses copied text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs out of caveman-managed files
Add a one-line provenance banner to any copied content
Review MCP inputs before execution
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported notes
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents are local-only on network egress, but caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, which can expose whatever is shared into its workspace. ai-engineering-hub has no data classes touched, so the leakage path is one-way and inferred from caveman’s documented file surfaces rather than direct evidence.
conditions: IF sensitive material from ai-engineering-hub is copied into caveman file surfaces
IF caveman persists session logs or memory files containing that material
mitigations: Do not copy secrets into caveman files
Store sensitive notes outside shared workspaces
Rotate or redact session logs after use
Restrict file permissions on project notes
requires-engineering: separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub shows no write surfaces or permissions, while caveman supports multiple instances but lists no elevated privileges or OAuth scopes. A write-conflict pathway is not documented, so only a limited overlap via shared files is plausible and the blast radius is small in the available evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF caveman instances modify the same file concurrently
mitigations: Avoid shared writable directories
Run one caveman instance per workspace
Use file locks for shared notes
Check in changes before launching another instance

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman exposes writing-oriented surfaces and multiple API integrations, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub outputs as authoritative notes, downstream actions could propagate errors. ai-engineering-hub is a content source rather than a verified executor, and no verification step is documented between them, so the cascade is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF caveman uses ai-engineering-hub output as source material for project notes or generated content
IF no human or automated verification step checks the imported claims
mitigations: Require source checking before reuse
Mark imported text as untrusted
Add a review step before publishing outputs
Limit caveman to drafting, not acting
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source docs-only with no secrets handled. Because the relevant compliance fields are absent, the pairwise compliance risk is limited to documentation gaps rather than a concrete violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into caveman's file surfaces
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not documented here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared notes
Document retention expectations
Review data handling before deployment
Keep secrets out of both repos
